Criteria:
- E1: Completeness: is every requirement, constraint and deliverable that the document states listed? For each missing one, quote its exact sentence from the document as evidence.
- E2: Faithfulness: is every listed item actually required by the document (not invented, not background, not a reading instruction)?
- E3: Kind: requirement = what the solution or the work must do or be; constraint = a limit on how or with what (language, library, team size, deadline, page limit); deliverable = what to hand in. Is each item the right kind?
- E4: Priority: must (must, shall, required, a plain instruction), should (should, recommended), could (may, optional, extra credit). Is each requirement's priority right?

Conventions (the same as the extractor's): one item per sentence or list item; setup steps that are not marked or checked (install a tool, clone a repository, create an environment), background, motivation and reading instructions are NOT items; a sentence ending with ':' that introduces a list is not an item, the list items under it are. Marking tables and their criteria (E ids) are checked by code: do not report them.

## IT 314 Assignment 2: Multi-client Chat Server
This assignment asks you to build a small chat system that many clients can use at the same time. Read the whole brief before you start.
## 1. Functional requirements
- The server must accept at least 10 clients connected at the same time.
- Each client must choose a unique nickname when it connects.
- A message sent by one client must be delivered to every other connected client.
- The server shall announce when a client joins or leaves the chat.
- Clients should be able to send a private message with the command /msg .
- The server may keep a history of the last 50 messages for new clients.
## 2. Quality requirements
- The server must not crash when a client disconnects without warning.
- Messages should reach other clients within one second on a local network.
## 3. Constraints
- Use Python 3.11 and the standard library only.
- Use TCP sockets; do not use a web framework.
- Work in groups of at most two students.
## 4. What to submit
- A ZIP file with the source code of the server and the client.
- A README that explains how to run both programs.
- A two-page report describing your design and how you tested it.
Submit everything on the course portal before 23:59 on Friday of week 6.
## 5. Marking
| Criterion | Marks |
|---|---|
| Correct message broadcasting | 30 |
| Nicknames and join/leave notices | 15 |
| Private messages | 15 |
| Robustness to disconnects | 20 |
| Code quality and README | 10 |
| Design report | 10 |
Total: 100 marks
Late submissions lose 10 % per day. This note is information, not a requirement for your program.
